sentences.text:
Ku.Sona Bai vs Kripal Singh on 7 October, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:53158
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Himanshu Joshi

On The 7 th Of October, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 1202 of 2006
 Ku.Sona Bai
 Versus
 Kripal Singh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Sanjay Kumar Saini - Advocate for the petitioner
 Smt. Amrit Kaur Ruprah, learned counsel for the respo
 Order

The present Misc. Appeal is being preferred taking exception to the provisions of section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, whereby the award dated 19/12/2005 passed in Claim Case no. 132/2004 by Learned IInd Additional Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Mandla has been challenged.

entities.text: IInd Additional Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Mandla
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The insurance company has also filed a counter-claim in the present appeal challenging the award.
2. The present appeal has been filed at the instance of the original claimant before the Tribunal for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The Learned Tribunal after evaluating the evidence and documents brought on record has passed an award of Rs. 54,000/- in favor of the appellant, herein.

3. The facts of the case reveals that the claimant has approached the learned Tribunal under the provisions of section 166 of the Motor Vehicles NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:53158 2 MA-1202-2006 Act.

entities.text: Motor Vehicles NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:53158 2 MA-1202-2006 Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The date of the accident was 06/11/2002 and the offending vehicle is Swaraj Tractor-trolly bearing no. MP-51-M -0704.
The offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1 and owned by respondent no. 2.
As per the claim petition, the appellant was sitting on tractor-trolly, which was going to carry murram.
The respondent being driver caused the accident while driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
The appellant sustained grievous injuries on both legs and back got fractured.
An FIR at Crime No.116/2002 was registered and Criminal case No. 445/2002 was set to motion before the trial court.
The appellant has filed claim petition for grant of Rs.3,30,000/- as compensation against the respondents.

Before the tribunal,
the respondents No. 1 and 2 remained ex parte.
The Insurance company has filed reply and contested the claim petition.
4. The tribunal after evaluating the oral testimony of the witnesses and also documents brought on record has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding Rs.54,000/- as compensation.

This order is Ku.Sona Bai vs Kripal Singh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45637259/
1 challenged in the present proceedings.

5. Shri Sanjay Kumar Saini, learned Counsel for the appellant criticizing the award amount has argued that the award has been passed on the lower side looking to the injuries sustained to the appellant.
It was also submitted that the award has been passed taking into consideration the Notional Income while monthly income to the tune of Rs.2,000/- has been assessed.
It has been submitted by the learned counsel that the injuries sustained are grievous in nature, which deserve enhancement.

6. Smt. Amrit Kaur Ruprah, learned counsel for the respondent NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:53158 3 MA-1202-2006 No.3/Insurance company has challenged the impugned order by filing Cross objection under Order XLI Rule 22 of the CPC.
It has been argued that the award has been wrongly passed.
The tractor is registered and insured as an agricultural vehicle and was being used contrary to the policy conditions.
She has relied upon a judgment of Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Vs. V. Chinamma and Others , reported in (2004) 8 SCC 7.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Vs. V. Chinamma and Others , reported in (2004) 8 SCC 7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard the parties at length, perused the impugned order and the material available on record.
8. The Learned Tribunal has framed five issues in the matter.
Issue No. 1 pertains to the mode of the accident, which was found proved by the Tribunal.
Issue No. 2 is related to the coverage of the insurance policy of the offending vehicle.
This issue was required to be proved by the insurance company; however, it was not proved.
Issue No. 3 is concerned with the violation of any policy conditions or license requirements with respect to the offending vehicle.
This issue was also found not proved, meaning thereby the offending vehicle was not plying in contravention of the license conditions.
Issue No. 5 is related to the determination of compensation, and the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.54,000/- in favour of the claimant.
In the opinion of this Court, the learned Tribunal, after duly appreciating the nature of the injuries sustained, has rightly concluded and granted compensation to the tune of Rs.54,000/-.
The same does not warrant any interference considering the facts and circumstances of the case.

9. The Insurance Company has filed a cross-objection in the matter NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:53158 4 MA-1202-2006 on the ground that the appellant was traveling in the tractor as a passenger, which was in breach of the policy conditions, as the tractor was insured for agricultural purposes and not for carrying passengers or goods.
However, the evidence on record clearly indicates that the Insurance Company failed to prove that the offending vehicle was being used in contravention of the terms of the insurance policy.
It thus follows that the appellant was traveling in the tractor as a passenger, even though the tractor was designed to accommodate only one person, namely, the driver.
Therefore, the Insurance Company (respondent No. 3) cannot be held liable for the loss or injuries suffered by the appellant, nor to indemnify the owner of the tractor.

10. However, in the facts of the present case the Insurance Company is directed to pay the compensation amount to the claimant (appellant) with liberty to recover the same from the tractor owner, in view of the consistent view taken in that regard by this Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Ku.Sona Bai vs Kripal Singh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45637259/
2

entities.text: Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Ku.Sona Bai vs Kripal Singh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insurance Co. Ltd. (2018)5 SCC 656, Rani & Ors.
Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors. (AIR online 2016 SC 297) and including Manuara Khatun and Others Vs. Rajesh Kumar Singh And Others.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors. (AIR online 2016 SC 297)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manuara Khatun and Others Vs. Rajesh Kumar Singh And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Looking to the facts and circumstance of the present case, the cross objection of the insurance company is partly allowed and the appeal preferred by the claimant is dismissed.
The Respondent no. 3 may, therefore, succeed in getting relief of direction to pay the compensation amount to the appellant with liberty to recover the same from the tractor owner (respondent No.2).

12. Reverting to the issue regarding the determination of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:53158 5 MA-1202-2006 compensation amount by the tribunal, this court find that the tribunal had taken into account all the relevant aspects provided for just and proper compensation amount for different heads as are permissible.
The Court, therefore, feels it justified in not disturbing the said conclusion of the tribunal.
Accordingly, the appeal preferred by the appellant for enhancement of compensation amount does not warrant interference.
13. This appeal is disposed of with the aforesaid direction.
There shall, however, be no order as to costs.

(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE Jasleen Ku.Sona Bai vs Kripal Singh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45637259/
3
